note: 🌓️ What the pre-paint appearance bootstrap must resolve, stated once and answered twice. The head's inline `<script>` runs BEFORE any module is fetched, so the appearance it resolves is the one the very first painted frame uses — resolve it wrong and a dark session flashes light on every reload. `storageKey`/`preferenceKey` name the ONE durable document the OS shell writes (`OS_SHELL_CONFIG_STORAGE_KEY`, `UI_PREFERENCES_CONFIG_SCHEMA`); `events` is the append-only UI-preference log exactly as `commitUiPreferencesConfigMutation` persists it, so a case is a replay, never a state blob. `deadKeys` names storage keys the bootstrap must NOT read: they were written by a shell generation that no longer exists, and reading one is how the regression this fixture closes happened in the first place. The TypeScript half EXECUTES the shipped script string in a DOM-less sandbox; the Rust half replays the same events through the OS config projection and answers only the appearance. Ticket 26/09/09/PROCEDURAL-3D-END-TO-END.

cases.name: a first visit follows the system, dark
a first visit follows the system, light
a dark session on a light system boots dark — the regression this fixture closes
a light session on a dark system boots light
the LAST setAppearance wins — the log is replayed, not merged
an explicit return to system follows the system again
a log carrying no appearance at all follows the system
a corrupt document never throws in the head and falls back to the system
